name: Forms and Checkout Rulebook
summary: Forms people can finish: fields, labels, validation, errors and checkout.
check: Fill every form with the keyboard and with browser autofill.
Submit with errors: values kept, messages next to fields, focus moves to the first error.

rules.title: One column
rules.text: Forms run in a single column, in the order people think about the information. Short related fields (city and postcode) may share a row.

rules.title: Labels above fields
rules.text: Every field has a visible label above it, always visible while typing (`IX-11`).

rules.title: Mark both required and optional
rules.text: Mark required fields and optional ones explicitly, so nobody has to guess.

rules.title: Autocomplete and the right keyboard
rules.text: `autocomplete` tokens (name, email, tel, street-address, postal-code, cc-number) and `inputmode` on every field, so browsers fill them in and phones show the right keyboard.

rules.title: Validate after leaving the field
rules.text: Check a field when the user leaves it and on submit, not on every keystroke. Show success quietly and errors next to the field.

rules.title: Error summary on long forms
rules.text: After a failed submit of a long form, list all errors at the top with links to each field, and move focus there.

rules.title: Keep everything on error
rules.text: A failed submit keeps every value, including payment fields where allowed (`IX-14`).

rules.title: Guest checkout first
rules.text: Shops let people buy as a guest as the most prominent option and offer an account after the order.

rules.title: Full price early
rules.text: Shipping, taxes and fees are visible in the cart, before the payment step.

rules.title: Named steps in multi-step forms
rules.text: Multi-step forms show the steps by name ("Delivery", "Payment") with the current one marked. No step numbers (`SL-17`).

rules.title: Show password option
rules.text: Password fields have a show/hide toggle and accept paste and password managers.

rules.title: Address lookup where it helps
rules.text: Offer address autocomplete or postcode lookup, with manual entry always possible.

rules.title: Placeholder as the label
rules.text: Never use placeholder text as the only label. It disappears while typing and has poor contrast.

rules.title: Asking for what is not needed
rules.text: No title, gender, birth date, company or phone unless the task truly needs it now (`SL-47`).

rules.title: Forced account creation
rules.text: Never require an account to buy, book or download something.

rules.title: Splitting simple fields
rules.text: Do not split names, phone numbers or dates into several boxes unless the format really requires it.

rules.title: CAPTCHA by default
rules.text: No puzzle for every visitor. Use invisible protection (honeypot, time check, rate limits) and show a challenge only on suspicious traffic (`SEC-08`).

rules.title: Clearing the form or resetting it
rules.text: No "Reset" button, and never clear fields after an error or a session timeout.
